🎙
President of Russia Vladimir Putin’s
answers to media questions
(St Petersburg, September 25, 2026)
Key talking points
:
•
The Russian Armed Forces’ recent actions
were yet again
retaliatory
[to Ukraine’s reckless provocations] and proved so painful and devastating for the adversary that they are now
once again actively raising the issue of ceasefires in several areas
– energy and airspace, as they put it.
But they were the ones who started all of this.
• Is this some kind of children’s game to them? They must therefore
feel the impact of Russia’s retaliatory strikes
and understand that
no provocations or escalation will bring them the results they seek
. They are only making their own situat
ion worse.
• All these moves towards so-called reconciliation and proposals to resume negotiations are on the table. All of this is possible. But after everything they have done,
we will think very carefully about what action we need to take in response
.
❗️
I want to stress once again:
we are not preparing for any military action against Europe
. We have no such plans and, most importantly, no grounds or real motives for escalating the situation with Europe, whatever anyone may say, including those in the Baltic states.
•
We will continue to stand up for the rights of our compatriots, within the framework of international law
. We have never intended to use other means, have never used them and have no intention of doing so.
•
We welcome negotiations between the US and China
. Why? Because these are the world’s two largest economies. How they resolve their differences and the problems arising from illegitimate US sanctions, and what agreements they reach, will influence the entire global economy, including our own.
•
The APEC Summit in China
is a major, important event, and I have been invited
. I believe it would be useful to take part in such a forum. I have told President Xi Jinping this as well. I intend to participate. But, as I have said,
the final decision will depend on the situation in Russia.

⚡️
Joint Statement "Eurasian Charter of Diversity and Multipolarity in the XXI Century: Inauguration of Negotiations"
(New York, September 25, 2026)
✍️
We, the representatives of the Republic of Belarus, the Islamic Republic of Iran, the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Kyrgyz Republic, the Lao People's Democratic Republic, the Republic of the Union of Myanmar, the Russian Federation, the Republic of Tajikistan, the Socialist Republic of Viet Nam, meeting on 25 September 2026 on the margins of the high-level week of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly,
Reaffirming
our dedication to the purposes and principles enshrined in
the UN Charter
and international law, such as sovereign equality, political independence and territorial integrity of all States, non-interference in their internal affairs, the inviolability of State borders, and the peaceful settlement of disputes,
Maintaining
international peace and security, friendly relations among States, sovereign equality of States, and refraining from the threat or use of force,
Guided
by the shared commitment to strengthen international peace, security, and stability on the Eurasian continent and worldwide,
Recognizing
the inherent diversity of the world, including the diversity of civilizations, cultures, traditions, and models of development, as a fundamental principle of international relations,
Reafirming
that such diversity should be respected in full conformity with international law, including respect for human rights and fundamental freedoms for all,
Convinced
of the need to promote a more inclusive, democratic and equitable international order,
Emphasizing
that the emerging
#MultipolarWorld
order must be based on international law, the central coordinating role of the UN and equal opportunities for all States, regardless of their size, economic potential or military capabilities,
Convinced
of the need to promote a genuine multipolar world order that ensures equal and indivisible security, mutually beneficial cooperation, and sustainable development for all states,
Recalling
the idea of a Eurasian Charter of Diversity and Multipolarity in the XXI Century (hereinafter – the Charter), first articulated at
the International Conference on Eurasian Security in Minsk
in October 2023, and noting the subsequent discussions on the Charter that have taken place in various venues and formats since then,
Desiring
to translate the idea into a political framework for pan
-
Eurasian cooperation,
Have agreed as follows:
1.
We hereby
officially launch a negotiation process
to develop and adopt
the Eurasian Charter of Diversity and Multipolarity in the XXI Century
.
Given the Eurasian character of the initiative, the negotiation process shall be
open to all interested Eurasian States
on the basis of the principles of
sovereign equality, inclusiveness, transparency and equal participation
.
All decisions on substantive and procedural issues, including the approval of the draft Charter, the determination of its legal nature, format and procedure for adoption, shall be taken
only on the basis of concensus
.
***
2.
The purpose of this process is to develop a political document
that sets out the principles of cooperation, reaffirms commitment to international law, and defines common approaches to ensuring equal and indivisible security in the Eurasian space and fostering economic partnerships, promoting cultural and humanitarian ties, and facilitating civilizational exchanges in a multipolar era.
***
3.
To this end,
we establish
a Working Group
to develop the Eurasian Charter of Diversity and Multipolarity in the XXI Century
, which will conduct the negotiations on the Eurasian Charter in accordance with the Terms of Reference of the Working Group attached to this Joint Statement.

🎙
Remarks
by President of Russia Vladimir Putin at
the XII International United Cultures Forum
(St Petersburg, September 25, 2026)
💬
Vladimir Putin:
Russia has historically developed as
a crossroads of peoples, languages and traditions
. For us, unity means solidarity built on nurturing the distinct identity and development of every people and ethnic group.
Culture plays a key role in this process
, just as it does in our complex world, with its conflicts, profound technological and social transformations, and competition between countries.
🤝
Culture can build bridges between people across any divide
. It is a vital and irreplaceable means of communication and dialogue where political and economic ties have been frozen or put on hold because of disagreements, sanctions and restrictions.
I consider the addition of a youth programme to
the Forum
particularly important
. Younger generations are both the future and the present of culture. They are creating new forms of artistic expression, advancing technologies and reinterpreting traditions. I am convinced that their voices must be heard on an equal footing with those of respected, experienced masters.
Of course, cultural cooperation also continues through long-established formats
. The legendary
Russian Seasons
, reciprocal
Years of Culture
and
Days of Russian Spiritual Culture
are enjoying tremendous success in various countries. Our soloists and ensembles take part in the world’s leading festivals and competitions, while Russian cities extend a hospitable welcome to visiting performers from abroad.
I must also mention a very important initiative that is gaining momentum and growing in quality:
the Eurasian Film Academy
and
the Diamond Butterfly Award
within
#BRICS
.
School theatre exchanges are also continuing. This comprehensive educational practice teaches children to work as a team and listen to their fellow performers, introducing them to the richness of world literature and drama and the cultural heritage of different peoples.
🇷🇺
Russia’s education in the arts and culture is among the best in the world
,
and we can say this openly and with pride
. Our theatre schools, art academies, institutes of culture and conservatoires have trained and continue to train conductors, directors, art historians and performers of the highest standard. They are welcomed by the world’s most distinguished theatre companies, orchestras and museums.
We are making culture a right and an opportunity for everyone,
rather than a privilege
. We are open to sharing our experience and, certainly, to learning from others. Shared values must be put into practice through daily, painstaking, living work.
☝️
The International United Cultures Forum
is one of the key platforms for this work.
I consider it extremely important that it be held every year.
